brief.title: Choose a workshop label system
brief.question: Which label system best fits our small workshop's budget and planning horizon?
brief.background: Entirely fictional sample. These values are arithmetic fixtures, not supplier quotes or market estimates.
brief.goal: Replace handwritten labels with a repeatable label system for workshop orders.

options.label: Option A · lower upfront
consequences: Lower initial commitment; monthly costs accumulate faster.

options.label: Option B · lower recurring
consequences: Higher initial commitment; lower recurring cost.

options.label: Keep handwritten labels
consequences: Reversible and avoids a purchase; does not meet the stated replacement goal.

hard_requirements.description: All-in cost must remain within USD 2,500 over the chosen horizon.
Replace handwritten labels with a repeatable label system.

preferences.description: Prefer the lower comparable cost after hard requirements are met.
Prefer a smaller initial commitment when costs are otherwise comparable.

user_facts: Fictional scenario: both purchased systems meet the stated workflow need.
Tax, delivery, maintenance and installation are explicitly included at zero additional cost in the complete fictional quotes.
Keeping the current workflow is feasible but does not achieve the replacement goal.

evidence.text: Option A costs USD 1,000 upfront and USD 50 per month. Installation, delivery, tax and maintenance are included at zero additional cost. It meets the specified replacement workflow.
evidence.scope: Arithmetic and interface demonstration only; no real supplier or independent verification.

evidence.text: Option B costs USD 1,600 upfront and USD 20 per month. Installation, delivery, tax and maintenance are included at zero additional cost. It meets the specified replacement workflow.
evidence.scope: Arithmetic and interface demonstration only; no real supplier or independent verification.

evidence.text: Replace handwritten labels with a repeatable label system. The all-in budget is USD 2,500 over the selected horizon. Prefer the lower comparable cost. The existing handwritten approach requires zero new spending but does not meet this replacement goal.
evidence.scope: Arithmetic and interface demonstration only; no real supplier or independent verification.

evidence.text: Changed-input example only: Option B's required installation amount is omitted. USD 1,600 upfront and USD 20 per month are known, but the all-in cost remains unknown until installation is quoted. It continues to meet the specified replacement workflow.
evidence.scope: Arithmetic and interface demonstration only; no real supplier or independent verification.

contributions.summary: A fits the 12-month plan with the smaller initial commitment.
contributions.public_rationale: Using only the brief and shared cost snapshot, A costs USD 1,600 over 12 months. It meets the replacement goal in this fictional case. Keep the current approach as a deliberate defer alternative.
assumptions: All specified quote components are complete in the base fixture.

contributions.summary: The planning horizon is decisive: B becomes cheaper after month 20.
contributions.public_rationale: Using the same shared inputs, B's USD 600 higher upfront cost is offset by USD 30 per month in savings. This makes the break-even horizon 20 months. At 12 months, B costs USD 1,840.

claims.proposition: The complete A/B costs are equal at 20 months.

contributions.summary: Check all-in quotes; an omitted installation charge must remain unknown.
contributions.public_rationale: Both purchases meet the fictional workflow requirement. Their price ordering depends on the horizon and complete charges. Keeping handwritten labels avoids new spending but fails the replacement goal. Agreement among these manually authored fixtures does not verify real supplier facts.
open_questions: Will real quotes preserve the complete-cost assumptions?
